model.name: Server scale-invariance — per-request compute is O(children) never O(total-units) (shared warm index; achievable latency bound; discovered by measuring compute-vs-corpus)
model.description: SERVER SCALE-INVARIANCE: a per-request response path's server COMPUTE must be O(children)/O(1), NEVER O(total-units). An O(total) cost is INVISIBLE behind small fixtures — it only appears at production scale (sibling of gate-with-representative-data). ROOT (P0-B residual, Tron's 'task does nothing for a minute'): server handlers do a FULL-INDEX SCAN per request — idx.list()+get each (~5777 reads) to compute one badge, and new ScenarioIndex(...) per call (cold cache every request). MEASURED breadth first-hand 2026-08-31: 18 idx.list() + 40 new-ScenarioIndex sites in server.ts = a recurring HAZARD CLASS, not one-off. ★ SCOPE THE HAZARD NOT THE ACTOR: the brief's specific line numbers (2992/2856) had ALREADY DRIFTED when measured = proof a line-list rots; the invariant is DISCOVERED by measuring compute-vs-corpus (grow the corpus -> a scale-invariant path stays FLAT), NEVER a hand-list of line numbers. CROSS-CUTTING FIX: one SHARED WARM ScenarioIndex (list/get cache reused) + a cached CR reverse-index, instead of new-per-request. Same scale-invariant family as R37.31 phantom-coverage-at-scale (compute-flat + coverage-flat as the corpus grows). Realistic bound: O(1) requests + O(children) compute + ~1 RTT floor (~80ms) => an ACHIEVABLE ~100-150ms AC, NOT a bare aspirational 100ms on O(total) that would sit RED forever and rot (aspirational-invariant trap).
